theory.intro: An outcome is a possible result of a chance experiment. Outcomes are **equally likely** when each has the same chance of happening. Assume the spinners in these questions are spun fairly.
facts: An **outcome** is one possible result of an experiment. The **sample space** lists all distinct possible recorded results without repeats. When asked to list all sector outcomes, include the label on every sector, including repeated labels.

A fair coin has $2$ possible results and a standard die has $6$. A spinner label can appear on more than one sector, so the number of different recorded results can be less than the number of sectors.
For repeated labels on equal sectors, compare how many sectors have each label. Equal numbers of sectors give equal chances; a label on more sectors is more likely.
With one different label on each sector, a larger sector gives that label a greater chance.
steps: Identify the result recorded in the experiment.
If asked for all sector or card outcomes, list every sector or card label, including repeats. If asked for the sample space, list every distinct possible recorded result once.
Decide whether the recorded results have the same chance. Compare the sizes of their sectors, or how many equal sectors carry each label.

workedExamples.question_text:
A fair coin is tossed once.
List all the outcomes and the sample space. Say whether heads and tails are equally likely.
workedExamples.solution_text:
The outcomes are heads and tails.
The sample space is $\{\text{heads},\text{tails}\}$.
Heads and tails are equally likely because the coin is fair.

(a) The possible results are green, blue, red and yellow.
Green appears on $3$ equal sectors, blue on $2$, and red and yellow on $1$ each.
The four results are not equally likely.
(b) The possible results are sun, moon and star.
Each label appears on $2$ equal sectors, so the three results are equally likely.

The possible results are leaf, acorn and flower.
Leaf covers a larger part of the wheel, so the three results are not equally likely.
Acorn and flower cover equal parts, so these two have the same chance.

(a) The outcomes are $3,6,9,12$.
Each number occupies one equal sector, so the four outcomes are equally likely.

(b) Both are correct. Each list contains every possible recorded number once. The order does not change the sample space.

workedExamples.question_text:
Four cards are labelled $5$, $10$, $15$ and an unknown number. One card is selected at random and its number is recorded. The sample space is $S=\{5,10,15\}$.
Aisha says the unknown number could be $10$. Leo says it could be $20$. Who is correct? Explain.

[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\fontsize{10}{12}\selectfont,text=black},draw=black]
\foreach \x/\lab in {0/5,1.4/10,2.8/15,4.2/?} {\draw (\x,0) rectangle ++(1.1,1.4);\node at (\x+0.55,0.7) {$\lab$};}
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
workedExamples.solution_text:
Only Aisha is correct.
A repeated $10$ leaves the sample space as $\{5,10,15\}$. A card labelled $20$ would add a new possible result.
The unknown number can be $5$, $10$ or $15$.

(a) The sector outcomes are $A,A,A,B,B,C$.
The sample space is $\{A,B,C\}$.

(b) No. A sample space lists each distinct possible recorded result once, even when its label appears on several sectors.

foundation.question_text:
A carnival spinner has $4$ equal sectors labelled north, east, south and west.
Record every possible outcome of one spin.
foundation.solution_text:
Each equal sector gives one possible result.
The outcomes are north, east, south and west.

foundation.question_text:
A prize wheel has $5$ equal sectors labelled $A$, $B$, $C$, $D$ and $E$.
List all outcomes of one spin.

A fair spinner has $3$ equal sectors labelled sun, moon and star.
Are the three outcomes equally likely?
foundation.solution_text: Yes. Each label appears on one equal sector, so no outcome is favoured.

foundation.question_text:
A number wheel has $6$ equal sectors labelled $2,4,6,8,10,12$.
Record all possible results of one spin.

A spinner has $4$ equal sectors labelled lion, bear, bear and whale.
The animal is recorded after one spin. List the sample space.
foundation.solution_text:
List each different animal once.
The sample space is $\{\text{lion},\text{bear},\text{whale}\}$.

foundation.question_text:
A fair wheel has $5$ equal sectors labelled diamond, oval, oval, cross and cross.
List all the sector outcomes and then list the sample space.
foundation.solution_text:
The sector outcomes are diamond, oval, oval, cross and cross.
The sample space is $\{\text{diamond},\text{oval},\text{cross}\}$.

foundation.question_text:
A two-sector spinner is labelled day and night.
List its outcomes.
foundation.solution_text: The outcomes are day and night.

development.question_text:
An $8$-sector fair wheel is labelled N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W and NW.
Record every outcome of one spin.
development.solution_text: The outcomes are N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W and NW.

development.question_text:
A wheel has $4$ equal sectors labelled amber, blue, coral and denim.
Explain why the recorded colours are equally likely.
development.solution_text:
Each colour occupies exactly one equal sector.
Therefore each colour has the same chance of being recorded.

development.question_text:
A wheel has four sectors.
Red covers half the wheel, while blue, green and yellow each cover one sixth.
List the possible colours and decide whether they are equally likely.
development.solution_text:
The possible colours are red, blue, green and yellow.
They are not equally likely because red covers a larger part of the wheel.

development.question_text:
A fair spinner has $4$ equal sectors labelled $1,1,2,3$, and the number is recorded.
List the possible recorded numbers and decide whether those numbers are equally likely.
development.solution_text:
The possible recorded numbers are $1,2,3$.
They are not equally likely because $1$ appears on two sectors, while $2$ and $3$ appear once each.

development.question_text:
Wheel A has $6$ equal sectors with six different labels.
Wheel B has $6$ equal sectors, but one label appears twice and another appears once.
Which wheel has equally likely recorded labels?
development.solution_text:
Wheel A has equally likely recorded labels because every label occupies one equal sector.
Wheel B does not because its repeated label is favoured.

development.question_text:
Four cards are labelled $3$, $6$, $9$ and an unknown number. One card is selected at random and its number is recorded. The sample space is $S=\{3,6,9\}$.
Lena says the unknown number could be $3$. Omar says it could be $12$. Who is correct?
development.solution_text:
Only Lena is correct.
Another $3$ does not change the sample space. A card labelled $12$ would add a new possible result.

development.question_text:
A fair spinner has $9$ equal sectors labelled dawn, dawn, dawn, midday, midday, midday, midnight, midnight and midnight.
List the sample space and decide whether the recorded labels are equally likely.
development.solution_text:
The sample space is $\{\text{dawn},\text{midday},\text{midnight}\}$.
Each label appears on $3$ equal sectors, so the recorded labels are equally likely.

mastery.question_text:
A fair wheel has $12$ equal sectors: $4$ labelled fern, $3$ labelled moss, $2$ labelled reed, $2$ labelled ivy and $1$ labelled ash.
List the sample space. Are all five labels equally likely? Which two labels have the same chance?
mastery.solution_text:
The sample space is $\{\text{fern},\text{moss},\text{reed},\text{ivy},\text{ash}\}$.
The five labels are not equally likely because they appear on different numbers of equal sectors.
Reed and ivy each appear on $2$ equal sectors, so they have the same chance.

mastery.question_text:
A wheel has $5$ sectors of equal size labelled $P,Q,R,S,T$.
Another wheel has sectors of different sizes with the same five labels.
Which wheel makes the five recorded labels equally likely, and why?
mastery.solution_text:
Only the first wheel does.
Its labels each occupy one equal sector; different sector sizes give the labels different chances on the second wheel.

mastery.question_text:
A fair wheel has $8$ equal sectors labelled $A,A,B,B,C,C,D,D$.
Record the possible letters and decide whether the letters are equally likely.
mastery.solution_text:
The possible letters are $A,B,C,D$.
Each letter appears on two equal sectors, so the four letters are equally likely.
